environmental.operating-temp: to 70 C - 325 A per panel at 45 C, de-rated to 200 A at 70 C; no lower limit is stated

management.alarm-contacts: Form C relay per side, 2 A at 30 VDC and 0.6 A at 60 VDC, on wire-wrap terminals

physical.overall-mm: 431.8 x 44 x 331 without brackets (17 x 1.75 x 13.0 in)
physical.weight-configured-scope: populated, 17.0 lb in the datasheet; unpopulated is 12.0 lb

power.input-dc: dual feed; maximum input load 325 A at 45 C per panel, de-rated to 200 A at 70 C; input wire 2/0 AWG to 350 MCM
power.output-breaker-max: 60 A single-pole; the UL rating holds to 48 A continuous per output
power.power-max-scope: the alarm card alone at 48 V (30 mA); 0.48 W at 24 V and 0.22 W at 12 V. THE MONITORING CARD ALSO DRAWS FROM THE A AND B FEEDS, and no document held states how much (gap monitoring-card-draw), so this figure is a floor for the panel, not its total. Separately the guide gives a nominal power LOSS of less than 45 W per side at 325 A and 48 V, which is heat in the conductors and not a draw.

base.description: The panel as it ships: no breakers, and a blanking cover over every position. Breakers are sold separately.

populated.description: All sixteen positions fitted with breakers behind their touch guards, as every product photograph shows the panel, with an invented spread of ratings. An illustration, not an orderable bundle.

with-fuses.description: Side A on breakers and side B on TPA fuses in their holders, to show the two things a position takes. An illustration; the vendor sells the holder and the fuses for this panel and publishes no standard fill.

datasheet.title: Amphenol Network Solutions 300CB08/nrg300CB08 8/8 Position Circuit Breaker Panel data sheet, 07.11.24 v.20

description: 1RU dual-feed DC circuit breaker panel with nrgSMART circuit monitoring, sensor version: the 300CB08 with a sensor card that measures feed and per-circuit current and voltage and reports over nrgNET to a controller panel or an external controller. Vertical dual-stud inputs and screw terminal-block outputs. Two isolated sides, each fed at up to 325 A and each distributing to eight plug-in breaker positions of up to 60 A.

gaps.note: each feed is two stud terminals, one BATT and one RTN, and no drawing or sentence held says which is the outer one: the input-lug figure of the guide (Fig. 2-7) carries no legend, and its rear photograph prints BATT and RTN beside the output rows only. Each side is one part, `input-a` and `input-b`, whose two terminals are `terminal-1` and `terminal-2` by position, not by polarity.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph that resolves the input legends, or the panel itself.

gaps.note: the TPA fuse holder, part 307492, is seated from three-quarter views only: its face is placed by eye and its size is borrowed from the breaker whose position it fits.

the power drawn by the nrgSMART card is stated nowhere in the datasheet, the installation guide, the controller datasheet or the two controller configuration guides; searched for mA, watt, consumption and current draw. `power-max-w` is the alarm card alone.
gaps.wanted: the controller and sensor card current at 12, 24 and 48 V.

gaps.note: the two five-way nrgNET connectors are drawn at a 3.81 pitch, read off five ways in about 20 on Fig. 3-7; no document states the header or its pitch.
gaps.wanted: the nrgNET header part number or pitch.

gaps.note: the two nrgTEMP probe jacks are drawn from a photograph; no document held names the jack, and the probe ends in a phone-style plug of no stated size.
gaps.wanted: the probe jack type and plug size.

alarm-enable.description: one eight-way DIP switch per side; a switch enables the alarm for the breaker position of the same number

alarms.description: the rear centre block: alarm relay headers, nrgNET IN and OUT, and two temperature probe jacks

breakers-a.description: side A breaker positions, numbered 1 to 8 left to right

breakers-b.description: side B breaker positions; the panel prints POS 1 at the centre end and POS 8 at the right

feeds.description: one feed per side, A and B, each a BATT and an RTN stud terminal; which terminal is which is a recorded gap

name: nrg300cb08-sens

breaker-ratings.note: ONE MODULE CARRIES ELEVEN RATINGS AS A FIELD. The datasheet sells breakers from 2 A to 60 A as eleven part numbers that differ in nothing but the figure printed on the handle, so they are one part with a `rating` field, set per position in a configuration. Each breaker ships with a touch guard seated on it, a separate part that a configuration can take off. The populated example is an invented load to show the field working; the vendor publishes no standard fill.

chassis.note: 431.8 wide is the 17.00 inch dimension on Fig. 3-1, between the bracket folds. 43.9 high is the 1.73 inch dimension on the side view; the datasheet rounds the same height to 1.75 inch (44 mm). 330.8 deep is the 13.02 inch dimension on the bottom view, Fig. 3-12, front of the metal to the rear; the datasheet gives 13.0 inch (331 mm). The same view gives 345.5 overall, the extra 14.7 being the front cover and breaker guards standing proud of the chassis front.

ears.note: NOT DRAWN. The panel ships with separate 19 inch and 23 inch mounting brackets (PMTG19, PMTG23) that bolt to the sides; Fig. 3-1 dimensions them at 482.6 and 584.2 over the body.

envelope-faces.note: Top, bottom, left and right are sized from the chassis. The bottom vent fields and its two ground bolts are placed from Fig. 3-12 at 1.336 px/mm, a coarse reading. The top is given the same two side fields the photographs show running the depth of the lid; their extent is estimated. The sides are placed from the side view, Fig. 3-4, at 1.717 px/mm: four bracket holes 29.1 apart starting 11.1 from the front, and a two-bolt ground landing 268.8 from the front. THE GROUND BOLTS ARE DRAWN ON THE STATED 5/8 INCH CENTRES, 15.875 apart (one pair, see ground-pairs), not the 18.3 the drawing measures, because the callout states the figure and the drawing is coarse. Each side carries one landing and the bottom a third; the guide says only one ground connection is required.

front.note: Breaker cells, thumbscrews, lamp holes, switch slots and the designation card slot are measured on Fig. 3-1. Sixteen cells 17.8 x 39.1 on a 19.81 pitch (39 px), the first at 14.2 and the ninth at 261.1, which mirror about the centre to a tenth. What is printed on the front comes from the front photograph in the same guide (Fig. 1-1) and its positions are fractions of the centre panel read off that photograph, which is taken from slightly above: the wording is as printed, the positions are approximate. The DC, alarm and electrostatic symbols are drawn as plain strokes in the places the photograph shows them; their exact artwork is not resolved at that size. The front prints in dark ink on the pale panel. THE MODEL LEGEND IS A JUDGEMENT: the photograph of a sensor panel in the guide (Fig. 1-3) shows the plain panel layout with a model name beginning nrg300CB08 at the top right, cut off by the frame. The full part number is printed here. Fig. 3-3, the sensor front view, draws a box at that place and a small square between the switch slots that no document names; they are taken to be the model and voltage legends.

front-cover.note: THE FRONT FACE IS A REMOVABLE COVER. The guide has a procedure for it (section 2.2.7): two thumbscrews release a bar that spans the front, with sixteen openings the breaker guards show through and the lamps, switch slots and card slot in its centre. It is drawn as the panel, not as a part, because the panel is never seen without it in service and the breakers, not the cover, are what a position holds. The slot under the lamps is the designation card holder the datasheet lists.

ground-pairs.note: EACH LANDING IS ONE PAIR, NOT TWO STUDS (#828, #830). The installation guide's three sets of 1/4-20 threaded holes on 5/8 inch centres are each the landing of one dual-hole lug, so each is common/ground-stud-pair-5-8-1-4@1, two 1/4-20 pan-head screws at exactly 15.875, the pitch of the stud-pair-5-8 interface (formerly two common/ground-stud@1 placements 15.9 apart). Each pair is placed at rotate 90, one screw above the other as the side view, Fig. 3-4, and the bottom view, Fig. 3-12, draw the landings, centred where the two studs' midpoint was. A two-hole lug seated on a pair leaves its wire down the face (toward the front on the bottom view); each screw still takes a single-hole lug on its own, which the guide also allows. The earth mark beside each side landing is centred on its pair, 1.8 lower than it sat beside the two studs.

ground-stud-size.note: the installation guide's specifications give the earth ground terminals as three sets of 1/4-20 threaded holes on 5/8 inch centres, bolted with washers to 50 in-lb, for a dual-hole compression lug on #6 to #1 AWG wire; its description says they take either a dual-hole or a single-hole lug and that only one ground connection is required: the `stud-size` of all three ground pairs, one on each side and one on the bottom.

lamps.note: Five lamps on a 12.7 pitch: A PWR, A ALM, nrg, B ALM, B PWR (Fig. 2-11 names them, Fig. 3-3 draws the five holes). PWR is green with its feed present and ALM red on an alarm, as on the plain panel. The nrg lamp is the monitoring card: the guide gives off, red, green and flashing red for the older nrg300CB08 in terms of nrgNET power, and the controller guide says the Identify button blinks it. Whether the sensor version keeps the older meanings is not stated; red, green and a blink are recorded and no more.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-10-05 for an end-of-life, end-of-sale or discontinuation notice for the 300CB08 and found none; the vendor product page lists it as current. The installation guide marks a different part, the original nrg300CB08, as EOL and replaced by the -SENS and -CTRL versions.

method.note: THE PLAIN 300CB08 WITH A SENSOR CARD. Front, top, bottom and sides repeat the readings amphenol-ns/300cb08 made; the guide gives this version its own front view (Fig. 3-3), which was looked at and not re-measured, and its own rear centre (Fig. 3-7), which was.

monitoring.note: nrgSMART measures feed and per-circuit current, voltage and two probe temperatures. The controller and sensor electronics are powered from the A and B feeds, not from nrgNET (the nrgSMART integrated controller system configuration guide 151881). NO DOCUMENT HELD STATES WHAT THEY DRAW: the only power figure is the alarm card, 1.44 W at 48 V, which is what `power-max-w` carries here as it does on the plain panel. That figure is therefore low for this device by the draw of its monitoring card.

ratings.note: The datasheet gives the maximum input load as 325A @ 45 C per panel. The installation guide prints the same row with its de-rating: 325A @45 C per panel (De-rated to 200A @70 C). That is the only temperature either document states for the panel, so it is what `operating-temp` carries: a ceiling with its two rating points, and no lower limit.

rear.note: Fig. 3-6 at 3.2006 px/mm, scaled on the symmetric extent of the drawing (98 to 1480 px) taken as the 431.8 body, which then reads 43.6 high. The right bracket of that drawing is cropped, so its 19 inch span could not be used as a second check the way the front one was. The outputs are printed 8 to 1 left to right on each bank. As seen from the rear the left bank is side B and the right bank is side A, because side A is on the left of the front. THE CENTRE BLOCK IS THE MONITORED ONE: Fig. 3-7 draws two five-way nrgNET connectors and two probe jacks under the alarm headers, where the plain panel has only the headers.

rear-cover.note: NOT DRAWN. A clear polycarbonate cover closes the whole rear over the input and output terminals (datasheet, Primary Features; guide Fig. 2-20). It is transparent and everything behind it is what the rear view shows.
